stories.primary_headline: 'If actors & leaders not safe, then what about citizens?': Firing at Tiger Shroff’s car makes Oppn question Maharashtra govt over law and order

primary_source.headline: 'If actors & leaders not safe, then what about citizens?': Firing at Tiger Shroff’s car makes Oppn question Maharashtra govt over law and order
primary_source.content:
Mumbai: The Opposition on Sunday criticised the Maharashtra government over the firing incident involving Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff’s car in Mumbai, alleging that law and order in the city and state had deteriorated.In a post on X, Congress leader Sachin Sawant said Mumbai appeared to be in the grip of chaos and accused Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, who also heads the Home Department, of failing to maintain law and order.Referring to the murder of former Maharashtra minister Baba Siddique, the firing outside actor Salman Khan’s residence and threats to actors and film producers, Sawant questioned the state government’s efforts to rein in anti-social elements.Fadnavis speaks to Tiger Shroff, asks Mumbai Police commissioner to nab actor's assailants quicklyHe said the situation had reached a point where people who had earlier compared Maharashtra with Bihar were now saying that even Bihar was better.According to police, actor Tiger Shroff escaped unhurt after gunmen opened fire at his car in Mumbai’s Juhu area on Sunday evening. His driver and an autorickshaw driver were injured in the incident, police said.Mumbai Congress president Varsha Gaikwad demanded that Maharashtra have a separate home minister, blaming Fadnavis for the situation.मुंबईत कायदा आणि सुव्यवस्थेचे धिंडवडे!आधी सलमान खानच्या घराबाहेर गोळीबार, त्यानंतर बाबा सिद्दीकी यांची हत्या आणि आता अभिनेता टायगर श्रॉफवर गोळीबार झाल्याची बातमी!मुंबईसारख्या देशाच्या आर्थिक राजधानीत एकापाठोपाठ एक अशा घटना घडत असतील, तर मुंबईकरांच्या सुरक्षेची जबाबदारी नेमकी…&mdash; Prof. Varsha Eknath Gaikwad (@VarshaEGaikwad) October 18, 2026
 

“Does Mumbai have law and order? Does the police still command the same authority and respect as before? Are criminals afraid of the police?” she asked in a video statement.The Lok Sabha member said the Congress had consistently demanded that Maharashtra have a separate home minister.“If actors and political leaders are not safe, what can we say about the safety of ordinary citizens?” she asked.NCP (SP) MLA Rohit Pawar said the incident came days after the recent killing of Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Pradeep Purnekar in Thane.The firing incident involving the actor’s car was alarming, although the actor escaped unhurt, Pawar said.He also said such incidents, including the firing outside the Juhu residence of filmmaker Rohit Shetty, in Mumbai, the country’s financial capital, could undermine investor confidence.Pawar said the home portfolio should be handed over to a “competent minister” if the situation had become difficult to handle.The incident took place near Pushpa Park under Juhu police station limits in the western suburb, and the chain of events leading to the incident is being pieced together, an official said."Shroff is safe and has not sustained any injuries in the firing incident," the official reiterated.

brief_bullets: AP News Hurricane Trudy lashes Mexico's Pacific coast, but is set to weaken tonight Hurricane Trudy strengthens to Category 2 as it approaches Mexico coast AP News Hurricane Trudy gains strength near Mexico's coast, but is expected to weaken by Sunday Hurricane warning in effect from Manzanillo to Cabo Corrientes as storm moves toward Pacific coastTrudy strengthened to a category 2 hurricane as it moved toward Mexico’s south-western and west-central Pacific coast on Saturday, the US National Hurricane Center said.

brief_bullets: Paris: France woke on Sunday to the wreckage of one of its most violent days of unrest in years after protests over high prices and public services left one demonstrator dead, hundreds of police injured and nearly 1,800 people arrested.

Nationwide demonstrations erupted into riots on Saturday, with a town hall torched, shops ransacked, and buildings covered in graffiti as violent groups clashed with police in cities across the country.
One protester died after suffering a cardiac arrest during demonstrations in Paris, where police made a record 855 arrests.
Across France, police detained some 1,800 people and more than 500 officers were injured, the interior minister said.
why_it_matters_bullets: Shifts federal policy priorities and legislative momentum ahead of upcoming electoral and administrative deadlines.

stories.primary_headline: Army officer’s wife booked in Jammu & Kashmir over alleged links with Chinese intelligence operatives

primary_source.headline: Army officer’s wife booked in Jammu & Kashmir over alleged links with Chinese intelligence operatives
primary_source.content: Srinagar: Jammu and Kashmir Police have booked the wife of a serving Army officer for alleged espionage-related activities involving foreign intelligence operatives, including those linked to China, with investigators examining research papers she allegedly prepared on sensitive defence and geopolitical issues.The woman, a freelance researcher from Telangana, has not been arrested, and a preliminary inquiry has not established that she shared sensitive information, official sources said on Sunday.The case was registered at Gandhi Nagar police station on Friday under the Official Secrets Act, 1923, and relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).She was questioned by a Deputy Superintendent of Police-rank officer following the registration of the FIR, according to a PTI report.'Espionage Alert': UK accuses China of using academics to spy on AI and other tech researchInvestigators are examining allegations that the woman was tasked with preparing analytical papers on subjects including Line of Control (LoC) dynamics in Jammu and Kashmir, critical infrastructure projects in Arunachal Pradesh and drone deployment, sources said.The assignments allegedly involved individuals linked to Chinese intelligence operatives, they said.According to reports, the woman is well-qualified, undertook an IT internship with the United Nations in 2023 and currently works as a freelance researcher.The investigation is seeking to establish the nature of her contacts with foreign entities and whether any information or material was communicated to them.The allegations have not been independently established, and police have not publicly detailed the evidence recovered or confirmed whether any classified documents were involved.The investigation comes months after a Delhi court acquitted five accused in a separate espionage case registered in 2015.The accused, including serving and former security personnel, had faced charges under the Official Secrets Act over allegations of passing information about Army and Border Security Force deployments in Jammu and Kashmir to Pakistan-based intelligence operatives.In its May 20, 2026, judgment, the court found that the prosecution had failed to establish that the documents allegedly recovered were classified official records and that protected information had been communicated to enemy agents. All five accused were acquitted.
